title: Borderless EU Lockdown Mode rewrite and customer-scoped permissions
creator: Aisha Gomez
description: Goal: Implement a hardened 'EU Lockdown Mode' runtime enforcement path and a lightweight customer-scoped permissions model to support strict European data residency requirements while preserving developer ergonomics. This ticket rewrites the existing soft-routing checks into a deterministic enforcement chain: (1) route evaluation (region + tier), (2) explicit customer allowlist/denylist overrides with approval metadata, (3) runtime circuit for enforced egress-blocking, and (4) deterministic fallback to compatible model variants (EU-hosted or on-prem images). The work includes runtime policy evaluators, a per-tenant metadata store, an opt-in admin approval flow, expanded audit events, integration tests, and a staged rollout plan with observability and rollback hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Policy evaluator returns a deterministic decision (allow, deny, route-eu, fallback-variant) for >99% of production traces in local replay test
Per-tenant allowlist/denylist stored in the metadata service and editable via console + admin API with audit entries
Runtime enforcer rejects non-compliant egress attempts with a standard error code (EU_LOCKDOWN_DENY) and increments guard counters
Fallback sequence chooses the first compatible EU-hosted model variant or on-prem image and does not expose non-EU egress endpoints
End-to-end tests for 3 customer scenarios (EU-only tenant, mixed-tenant with allowlist, emergency-override) pass in CI
Telemetry dashboards show policy decision distribution, per-tenant denies, and latency delta before/after enforcement
Security review completed and signed off by InfoSec; audit retention meets 13 months requirement

notes: Trade-offs discussed: strict enforcement at edge minimizes accidental egress but increases latency risk when fallback checks require remote compatibility calls. Mitigation: aggressive local caching + precomputed compatibility table populated by the model-onboarding pipeline.

Approval model: allowlist entries can be created by tenant admins but 'enforced_mode' can only be enabled via console escalation which creates an approval ticket and requires two approvers from Security/Compliance for P0 customers.
Fallback variants: prefer EU-hosted quantized variants (same family) > dedicated on-prem model > deny. All fallbacks are recorded with reason codes for post-incident review.

Emergency passthrough: temporary emergency-override tokens can be issued for up to 4 hours; these are audited and automatically expire. The emergency flow requires manual revoke capability in Console.
Edge cache TTLs: policy decision cache 30s; variant compatibility cache 10m. These are tunable via runtime flags for lower-latency tenants.

test_plan: Unit tests for evaluator decision table covering 48 permutations of headers, tenant policies, and model metadata
Integration test harness that replays production trace samples with policy enforcement toggled
End-to-end smoke that verifies KV cache persistence across fallback variant switch
Chaos test: simulate metadata store latency and verify graceful failure mode (fail-open only for P3 tenants, fail-closed for enforced tenants)
Security test: validate audit trail immutability and approval token expiry
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Increased p99 latency due to variant compatibility lookups. Mitigation: local compatibility cache + precompute table during model onboarding.
Risk: Misconfigured allowlists could silently deny traffic. Mitigation: console warning, dry-run mode, and a staged ramp with an explicit opt-in for high-impact tenants.
Risk: Emergency-override abuse. Mitigation: short TTLs on tokens, two-step approval, and alerting on usage patterns.
Risk: Audit data volume. Mitigation: configurable retention per customer and aggregated retention for analytics
